Three ants walk on a thin rod 100 cm long.
When an ant reaches either end of the rod it falls off. When two ants meet,
they BOUNCE: both instantly reverse direction, and each keeps its own speed.

Starting positions and velocities (positive = toward the 100 cm end):

- Ant A: at 10 cm, moving +3 cm/s
- Ant B: at 40 cm, moving -1 cm/s
- Ant C: at 80 cm, moving -2 cm/s

After how many seconds does the LAST ant fall off the rod? Give the exact
number of seconds.


When you are finished, output your final answer on its own line, as the last line of your response, in the exact format:
ANSWER: <your answer>

text:
Let's analyze the movement of each ant and determine when they fall off the rod. The rod is 100 cm long.

Ant A: Starts at 10 cm, moves +3 cm/s. It falls off if it reaches 100 cm or 0 cm.  The position of Ant A at time t is $x_A(t) = 10 + 3t$. It will fall off when $10+3t=100$, so $3t=90$ and $t=30$. Alternatively, it falls off when $10+3t=0$, so $3t=-10$ and $t=-\frac{10}{3}$, which is not a valid time since t must be positive. Thus Ant A falls off at t = 30 seconds.

Ant B: Starts at 40 cm, moves -1 cm/s. The position of Ant B at time t is $x_B(t) = 40 - t$. It will fall off when $40-t=100$, so $t=40-100=-60$ which is impossible since t must be positive, or when $40-t=0$, so $t=40$. Thus Ant B falls off at t = 40 seconds.

Ant C: Starts at 80 cm, moves -2 cm/s. The position of Ant C at time t is $x_C(t) = 80 - 2t$. It will fall off when $80-2t=100$, so $-2t=20$ and $t=-10$, which is impossible, or when $80-2t=0$, so $2t=80$ and $t=40$. Thus Ant C falls off at t = 40 seconds.

Since all three ants fall off the rod at the same time (t=40), the last ant to fall off is Ant C.

The last ant falls off the rod after 40 seconds.

ANSWER: 40
